newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says UK budget tightens fiscal policy.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says UK budget tightens fiscal policy.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke said on Tuesday his annual budget would tighten fiscal policy to reduce the chances of higher interest rates.

Clarke, presenting his budget to parliament, said he would propose measures to stem tax loopholes. Britain would in 1997 meet public debt and budget deficit criteria required for countries to enter a European single currency.
Clarke unexpectedly raised interest rates last month to six percent from 5.75 to douse down inflationary pressures.

Clarke said the budget would cut public spending by seven billion pounds ($11.69 billion) over the next three financial years. He expected public sector borrowing to be gradually reduced so as to be broadly eliminated by the 1999/2000 financial year. ($1=.5990 Pound)
